summary.headline: Jyothy Labs Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA margin fell to 2.5% from 16.1% as gross margin dropped to 34.8%, despite 3.3% revenue growth to INR760 crore.
summary.overview: Reported revenue rose 3.3% YoY to INR760 crore, but the Pril and Fa exit (brand licence expired May 2026) depressed reported volumes; excluding these brands, value grew 12.4% and volume 8.1%. Crude-linked raw material and packaging inflation compressed gross margin to 34.8% (48.1% last year, 38.5% in Q1), pushing operating EBITDA to INR19 crore and PAT to INR10.6 crore. Management took about 4% price increases, said pricing alone cannot close a 13-14% inflation gap, and called FY27 an aberration year. The Board approved a INR147 crore tender-offer buyback at INR215 per share, with promoters not participating.

segments.name: Fabric Care
segments.commentary: Led growth with 10.4% value growth; liquid detergents grew over 50% YoY (Henko, Ujala, MoreLight, Mr. White), and Ujala Young & Fresh fabric conditioner is performing well. Management said liquids carry lower margins than powder while the category scales.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Excluding Pril, segment grew 15.3%, mainly on volume. Exo dishwash grew 23% on new variants, liquids, wider distribution and brand investment.

segments.name: Household Insecticides (HI)
segments.commentary: Coil share of HI portfolio fell to 30-35% from 43-45% a year ago as liquid vaporisers, aerosols and other formats scale; Maxo Agarbatti launched with a government-approved formulation. Profitability improvement is the priority.

segments.name: Personal Care (Margo)
segments.commentary: Grew a little over 11% in value on Margo pricing and a favourable GST base. Price increases of about 10-12% in Margo could not fully absorb palm oil and neem oil inflation; Margo Gentle glycerin soap (argan and moringa variants) launched in select markets.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the underlying business to sustain healthy growth in Q3 FY27, led by Fabric Care and new products.
Gross margins expected to remain under pressure in Q3; a full H2 margin recovery cannot be assumed unless commodity prices moderate and stabilise.
Margin recovery to be progressive; management said pricing alone cannot bridge a 13-14% inflation gap, and recovery is expected to begin in H2 depending on commodity stability.
Effective tax rate for H1 was 28.4%; full-year rate expected around 25-26%.
Working capital expected to gradually return to the 18-20 day medium-term range as conditions stabilise.
Internal aspiration to keep delivering double-digit growth; FY27 described as an aberration year, and no formal guidance given. INR5,000 crore revenue aspiration remains unchanged.
Dividend payout policy of 35-50% of profit retained; buyback of INR147 crore at INR215 per share via tender offer.
capex_capacity: Capital allocation: INR147 crore tender-offer buyback approved at INR215 per share; promoters and promoter group will not participate.
Management said cash will go to dividends, acquisitions, and investment in NPDs and new categories; M&A remains open, with no deal-size or return thresholds disclosed.
Working capital rose to 23 days from 15 days in March, mainly from higher raw material and finished goods inventory valued at higher input costs; debtor days fell over the same period.
Packaging is about 18-20% of cost base; HDPE and polypropylene prices up about 55-60% from pre-West Asia conflict levels.
demand_pricing: Rural outperformed urban; modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce grew strongly (modern trade double-digit); general trade subdued.
Price increases of about 4% taken in the quarter; further selective pricing and grammage cuts, especially in lower unit packs, under evaluation while balancing affordability.
Crude-linked inputs are 60-65% of consumption basket; inflation hit LABSA, SLES, soap noodles, palm oil, neem oil and packaging.
Renewed inflationary pressure in October 2026 adds near-term uncertainty; commodity prices had softened in July and early August.

Employee costs about 12% of revenue (up about 5.7% YoY); advertisement and promotion 7.4% of revenue (about 100 bps higher QoQ); other expenses about 13% of revenue vs 12.1% last year, driven by freight and export shipping costs.

qa_highlights.question: What steps are being taken to restore historical margins, and are new product launches or higher advertising part of this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited NPDs with better margin profiles and a shift in product mix away from fixed-price LUPs, plus back-end cost efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the price increase only about 4% when peers have raised prices, and how much more is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Pawan Agarwal said RM and PM inflation cost about 18% of sales, offset by 4% price and some mix, a net 13-13.5% gross margin hit. Pricing alone cannot close the 13-14% gap; recovery will be progressive, combining pricing, procurement, value engineering and mix.

qa_highlights.question: Has the liquid detergent mix diluted fabric care margins, and how should H2 margins be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquids carry lower margins than powder while scaling and requiring consumer-conversion spend; the Fabric Care margin hit is mainly input cost. Management declined to guide, calling FY27 an aberration year and saying margin recovery should start in H2 if commodities stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR5,000 crore revenue aspiration be reached, given Pril's exit and M&A timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aspiration stands and M&A is not on hold; it is waiting for the right opportunity under a checklist. Growth will come from NPDs in categories not yet named, with launches in the last 2-3 years performing well.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Pril and Fa exit changed distributor terms, and what drove the working capital increase?
qa_highlights.answer: No change to distributor ROI or trade terms and no credit expansion; debtor days fell from March to September. The working capital increase is mainly raw material and finished goods inventory at higher costs.

qa_highlights.question: How does management view Margo's positioning in a crowded natural personal care segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said natural space still has loyal and young consumers, Margo will grow through extensions such as Margo Gentle, and other personal care opportunities will be addressed through other brands.

qa_highlights.question: Is crude dependence a major threat, and is management developing lower-crude products?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude-linked inputs are about 60-65% of the cost base. Management said R&D is developing lower-crude-dependence products with better margins, with some expected next year.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on commodity stability; October 2026 showed renewed inflation pressure.
Pril and Fa exit removes two brands from the base; growth now relies on Exo, Fabric Care, Margo and new launches.
Liquid detergents are margin-dilutive during scale-up; monitor the gap versus powder.
Working capital at 23 days vs the 18-20 day target; inventory at high input costs must unwind.
Affordability limits on pricing and grammage cuts may weigh on volumes and general trade demand.
Capital allocation between buyback, dividends and M&A; timing of any acquisitions is undisclosed.
Monsoon deficiency and rural purchasing power could affect H2 demand.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on profitability: management called the 2.5% EBITDA margin "significantly below our expectations" and declined to give formal guidance. It stayed confident on top-line momentum, Fabric Care and new launches, and framed the margin issue as temporary.
key_quotes: We recognize that this level of profitability is significantly below our expectations.
FY27 should be treated as an aberration year given the external environment, geopolitical situation and the input inflation, what we are seeing, what we are witnessing, which is unprecedented.
We do not see a structural deterioration in the economics of our business. It is a temporary issue, which is caused by inflationary trends in our key raw materials and packaging materials.
Margin recovery is likely to be progressive rather than immediate.
